newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER-FRENCH FAIL TO RESOLVE SCORING CONUNDRUM.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-FRENCH FAIL TO RESOLVE SCORING CONUNDRUM.

text.p: Despite the experimental nature of their Tournoi de France World Cup dress rehearsal, France can ill afford another poor result in their last match in Paris on Wednesday.
Aime Jacquet's side, beaten 1-0 by England on Saturday, stumbled again in their quest for an attack capable of leading them to their first World Cup title next year.
They have taken one point and scored one goal in their two matches yet, paradoxically, have the foundations of a very good team.
They have been beaten only twice in 36 matches, once away and once at home on Saturday.

Local crowds appreciate what Jacquet is trying to achieve but their calls for Ibrahim Ba, unheeded, and Zinedine Zidane, who came on 14 minutes from time, indicate that they know France's strengths and want them used.
"We have established a working plan and are sticking to it. This defeat is in no way worrying. We must be patient," Jacquet said.
The traditionally hard-to-please Paris crowd could, however, become impatient at the Parc des Princes on Wednesday if their team do not quickly go head against the Italians.
Should they lose and finish bottom in their tournament, Jacquet could face a stressful 12 months preparing for the World Cup finals.

"We have a big problem, we still take a half to get into the match," said Sampdoria utility defender Pierre Laigle, whose second half shot from outside the box which brought a superb save from David Seaman was France's best chance.
Jacquet said: "We still have a problem of finishing. But our presence in front of goal is interesting, especially in the second half. All we lack is sang-froid, lucidity.
"(Fabien) Barthez was exceptional for 89 minutes. He did not deserve that," added Jacquet of Alan Shearer's goal, scored in the 85th, taking advantage of the Monaco goalkeeper's only mistake.
Barthez said he and Laurent Blanc misunderstood each other over who was going for Teddy Sheringham's low cross.

France have found a good successor to Bernard Lama in Barthez, they have a sound defence and a balanced midfield that played very well in the second half against Brazil in Tuesday's opening match, laying on Marc Kellers's equaliser in a 1-1 draw.

Ba, a fast an tricky runner on the right, was the architect of Keller's goal but did not play against England chiefy because Jacquet knows what he has in the gifted AC Milan-bound player, preferring to try out new combinations that involved eight changes from the side that drew with the world champions.
"Against Brazil with two players on the wings (Ba and Pires, then Keller), we have answers," Paris St Germain striker Patrice Loko said.
Up front, France are struggling even if they scored five goals and conceded one in their first three games of the year prior to this tournament.
Jacquet appears to be finding it hard to give the talented Youri Djorkaeff his best role, starting him on Saturday in the Zidane position of playmaker behind two strikers.
When Zidane came on, France reverted to their Euro 96 format of a deep lying forward, Djorkaeff, complementing one out-and-out striker, at that point substitute Loko.
"People always try to dissociate us, Zidane and me. But when he came on, you saw a difference. He's the one with whom I have most relation," Djorkaeff said.
Earlier both Christophe Dugarry and Nicolas Ouedec found it very hard to make chances as a twin strike pair against a solid England back three, although the Milan man twice came close.
"Bravo Shearer. He kept at it and finally scored. I never had a similar ball," Espanyol's Ouedec said.
